title: Change of coefficients and base change for the diagonal class
statement:
1. Extension of scalars along $\Zl\to\mathcal O_E$ carries $\delta_{\Zl}$,
   $\operatorname{Tr}_q$ and the integration identities to $\mathcal O_E$-linear
   morphisms $\delta_{\mathcal O_E}$, $\operatorname{Tr}_q$ satisfying the same
   identities, whose reductions modulo $\pi_E^n$ (equivalently modulo
   $\ell^n$) are the torsion classes and traces.
2. Inverting $\ell$ and passing to the filtered colimit over finite
   extensions of $E$ inside $\Qlb$ gives $\delta_E$, $\delta_{\Qlb}$ and their
   traces, with the same identities.
3. For a separated morphism of finite type $g:Y'\to Y$ of the standing
   setting, the pullbacks of $\delta_\Lambda$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_q$ along
   the base changes of $g$ are the corresponding morphisms for $Y'$.

proof.text: (1) Use the finite free coefficient extension in [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](2) for $\mathbf Q_\ell\subset E$. Choosing a $\mathbf Z_\ell$-basis identifies the underlying scalar-extension functor with a finite biproduct functor $K\mapsto K^{\oplus [E:\mathbf Q_\ell]}$. Thus it is exact and commutes with products and the cone of $1-\mathrm{shift}$ defining the derived inverse limit. An additive derived direct-image functor preserves finite biproducts, so the canonical scalar/direct-image comparison is an isomorphism: in this basis it is the identity on each copy of $Rq_*K$, or $Rp_{i*}K$. Apply this functor to the class of [det-prop-diagonal-tower-limit](3), the traces and the equality of composites in [det-prop-diagonal-tower-trace](1),(2). This constructs the integral classes, traces and identities. The coefficient-ring limit is [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit](3). Writing $\ell=u\pi_E^e$ with $u$ a unit shows that the $\ell$-power tower is the cofinal subsystem of levels $en$ of the $\pi_E$-power tower. More explicitly, for every $m\ge1$, $A=\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^m$ is killed by $\ell^r$ for $er\ge m$. Reduction of the integral morphisms to $A$ is reduction modulo $\ell^r$ followed by derived extension along $\mathbf Z/\ell^r\to A$. The former reduction is given by [det-prop-diagonal-tower-limit](3) and [det-prop-diagonal-tower-trace](1); the latter is the torsion Cartier class by coefficient compatibility in [sk-lem-geo-cartier]. The torsion trace is the inverse of the unit/section decomposition followed by a summand projection, so extension of that finite biproduct decomposition carries it to the trace for $A$ of [sk-lem-geo-p1-cohomology]. This identifies every $\pi_E^m$ reduction, not just the cofinal levels.

source.place: paragraph (1): finite free extension, all quotient reductions and identities

proof.text: (2) By [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x], $E_X=\mathcal O_{E,X}[1/\ell]$ and $\QbarX=\varinjlim_{E\subset\Qlb}E_X$. Localization is the colimit of $K\xrightarrow{\ell}K\xrightarrow{\ell}\cdots$; composita make the finite-extension system filtered. Here the coefficient sheaves are in degree zero and their twists/shifts in degrees at least $-2$, a common lower bound. The maps $q,p_1,p_2$ are relative projective-line projections: over each affine open of the base they have the two standard affine charts, their overlap is affine, and their diagonal is cut out by $x_0y_1-x_1y_0$. Hence their inverse images of affine opens and their diagonals are quasi-compact, verifying the qcqs hypotheses directly. Apply [det-lem-bounded-continuity-direct-image] to the localization and finite-extension diagrams for these maps. Work with underlying abelian sheaves (so all diagrams have the common coefficient ring $\mathbf Z$). Filtered colimits are exact by [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaves-filtered-colimits-exact]; hence they commute with cohomology of complexes, and the canonical colimit/direct-image maps induce isomorphisms in every cohomological degree. Applying the coefficient colimits to the morphisms and composites in (1) therefore gives the $E$- and $\Qlb$-linear classes and traces and preserves both integration identities.

(3a) Put $P=\mathbf P^1_Y$, $W=P\times_YP$ and use primes for base changes to $Y'$. The diagonal has local equation $a-b$ in the chart where both projective coordinates have the same nonzero entry. Along the diagonal these charts cover it, and $a-b$ is monic in $a$, hence a nonzerodivisor over any base ring. The section $[1:0]$ has coordinate equation $t$ on its affine chart. These facts remain true over $Y'$, including nonflat base change, so all the relevant pulled-back divisors are Cartier. To compare the actual morphisms of systems of [det-prop-diagonal-tower-system], use its Cartier roof before reduction: pull units by $u\mapsto g^*u$ and the local Cartier generator by $t^{-1}\mapsto (g^*t)^{-1}$. A change $t\mapsto vt$ changes the latter generator by $(g^*v)^{-1}$, exactly the pulled-back relation; the maps glue and preserve the quotient generator $+1$. They give a commuting diagram of two-term Cartier complexes and their boundary roofs, with the natural map $g^{-1}\mathbf G_m\to\mathbf G'_m$ (no isomorphism of these multiplicative sheaves is assumed). Exact inverse image and compatibility with composition are [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image](4),(5). Apply the derived tensor functor to this single diagram, using the inverse-image/tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. At level $n$, the free resolution $[\mathbf Z\xrightarrow{\ell^n}\mathbf Z]$ has transition $\ell$ in degree $-1$ and $1$ in degree $0$; pulling this resolution preserves both maps. The root transitions are consequently $\zeta\mapsto\zeta^\ell$ on both sides. Thus the commuting diagram is a diagram in the derived category of systems, not an inference from equality of arbitrary derived maps at each level. The level classes and their coefficient compatibility are those of [sk-lem-geo-cartier].

source.place: paragraph (3), first sentence: explicit naturality of the Cartier and Kummer systems

proof.text: (3b) For a base-changed diagonal square, write $h:W'\to W$ and $h_D:P'\to P$. Its open complement is quasi-compact: on the displayed charts it is a principal open, and the projective charts form a finite cover over every base affine. The same holds after base change. The closed-support unit and counit in [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-abelian-closed-support] imply the required closed base change for any abelian coefficient sheaf $M$: $h^{-1}\Delta_*M$ restricts to zero on the complementary open (by the direct-image evaluation formula in [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image](2)), and its restriction to $P'$ is $h_D^{-1}M$, by composition of inverse images and the closed counit. The support unit therefore gives $h^{-1}\Delta_*M\simeq\Delta'_*h_D^{-1}M$. Apply this to $M=\mathbf Z/\ell^n$ and $M=\Zl$. The limit identifications in [det-prop-diagonal-tower-limit](1),(2) and the coefficient/twist identifications in [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](1) now show that the canonical comparison $h^{-1}R\varprojlim\to R\varprojlim h^{-1}$ is an isomorphism on both the source system $\Delta_*\mathbf Z/\ell^\bullet$ and the target system $\mathbf Z/\ell^\bullet(1)[2]$. Indeed on the supported source it is the just-displayed closed comparison, and on the target it is the coefficient/twist comparison. Naturality of this comparison applied to the single commuting diagram of (3a) gives $h^{-1}\delta_{\Zl}=\delta'_{\Zl}$ with the indicated source and target identifications. This only uses the two specified systems; no preservation of arbitrary inverse limits by inverse image is asserted.

source.place: paragraph (3): closed base change and the derived-limit comparison on the specified systems

proof.text: (3c) The schemes $Y,Y',P,P'$ are Noetherian: a field has only two ideals, and the finite-type-over-Noetherian theorem [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applies to their structure maps. At finite levels [sk-lem-geo-p1-cohomology] identifies the base-change map for $q$ with the direct sum of the coefficient comparisons on the unit and section-class summands. The section-class map as a morphism of systems is the one constructed in (3a), and the unit is natural by adjunction. Thus the base-change map carries the whole inverse-system decomposition of [det-prop-diagonal-tower-trace](1) to its primed decomposition. Applying $R\varprojlim$, which commutes with derived direct image by [det-prop-diagonal-tower-limit](1), reduces its comparison to the finite direct sum of the coefficient and twist comparisons of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](1). These comparisons are isomorphisms. Inverting the decomposition and projecting onto the twisted second summand commutes with this diagram, so the trace over $\Zl$ pulls back to the primed trace. For $p_i$, take the base $P$ in exactly this construction and its base-change map $P'\to P$; the same unit/diagonal-section diagram gives the asserted trace comparison for each $i$. Finally exact inverse image preserves colimits by [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image](3),(4), and its tensor comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], together with the coefficient identifications in [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-pullback], commutes with the finite free scalar extension, localization, and finite-subextension colimit of (1),(2). Applying those functors to the class and trace diagrams just proved gives the base-change assertion for $\mathcal O_E$, $E$, and $\Qlb$.

source.place: paragraph (3): trace decomposition comparison and subsequent coefficient changes

Exactness, colimits, composition, and the direct-image evaluation formula justify the inverse-image diagrams.
The generic monoidal derived pullback comparison supplies naturality of tensoring the Cartier complex and the coefficient stages.
Verifies the Noetherian hypothesis of the projective-line decomposition for the standing schemes.
